sections.crash_profile: During {{window_start}} to {{window_end}}, {{total_3y}} crashes occurred at this signalized four-leg intersection. There was {{ka_3y}} fatal or serious injury crash, with most injuries being suspected minor or possible. Left-turn opposing crashes were the most frequent, followed by rear-end and angle crashes. Nighttime and wet conditions contributed to a notable share. Pedestrian and bicycle counts are not available.
sections.why_flagged: Flagged due to a model-estimated fatal or serious injury crash rate of {{fsi_rate}} per mile and {{annual_fsi}} per year. Additional risk factors include high traffic exposure ({{aadt}} vehicles/day), four-leg signalized layout, proximity to school, and inclusion in the high-injury network. The site ranks {{rank_city_actionable}} among actionable city sites for crash risk.

countermeasures.rationale: Providing a left-turn lane on one major-road approach addresses the high frequency of left-turn opposing crashes. The cited CMF {{cmf:267}} is a direct crash-type match for this intersection configuration, but requires engineering review for severity scope and prerequisites.

Modifying change plus clearance intervals to the studied ITE 1985 practice may help reduce rear-end and angle crashes. The cited CMF {{cmf:380}} is a direct match for signalized intersections but needs engineering review for area setting and severity scope.

sections.benefit_cost: A benefit could not be computed for either countermeasure. The library lacks audit-approved CMFs with planning-level unit cost or service life, and the severity scopes do not match fatal or serious injury crashes only.
sections.next_steps: Conduct engineering review for left-turn lane feasibility and signal timing modifications, including geometry, traffic volumes, and existing equipment. Verify prerequisites and severity scope for each countermeasure. Complete source verification and coordinate with TxDOT as needed.
